_comment: Golden vectors for the Claude Code env-var spec (dev-docs/env-vars-pane-plan.md WI-1).
HAND-AUTHORED expectations, never generator output — a generated vector would only
lock in whatever the classifier already says. Both scripts/build-cc-env-spec.py and
claudepot-core::cc_env::spec run these, so the Python producer and the Rust consumer
Coverage: every control class; all 18 variables the previous generator classified as
tri-state toggles, each re-adjudicated by hand against its official prose; the two
SAFE_ENV_VARS-and-secret overlaps; each hazard class with a documented row; both
blocked reasons; the enum superset fix; the value set that must NOT be closed.
Assert only the fields a vector is about. Every listed field must match exactly.

vectors.name: MAX_THINKING_TOKENS
vectors.why: Re-adjudicated tri-state #1. A token budget whose doc names a ceiling (the model's max output tokens minus one). 'Set to 0 to disable thinking' is prose for a number whose zero is special, not a switch. A toggle here would write 1 into a budget.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS
vectors.why: Re-adjudicated tri-state #2. Doc states 'default: 120000, or 2 minutes' — a duration, not a flag.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT
vectors.why: Re-adjudicated tri-state #3. 'Idle timeout in milliseconds'. The name has no numeric suffix (_TIMEOUT is not one), so the millisecond prose is the load-bearing evidence — this vector guards that branch.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS
vectors.why: Re-adjudicated tri-state #4. 'Default: 600000, or 10 minutes'.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP
vectors.why: Re-adjudicated tri-state #5. 'Maximum number of consecutive times ... (default: 8)'. A count.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG
vectors.why: Survivor #1, and the case rev 2 got wrong by calling it a number. Its doc defines all three states: unset ('on by default'), 0 ('force-disable'), 1 ('force-enable'). A genuine tri-state.

vectors.name: API_FORCE_IDLE_TIMEOUT
vectors.why: Survivor #2. Reads like a duration but is not: 0 disables the timeout, 1 forces it on for every provider, unset is provider-dependent. The value is never a number of anything.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER
vectors.why: Survivor #3. 1 renders screen-reader output, 0 forces it off even when axScreenReader is true.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_AUTO_OPEN
vectors.why: Survivor #4. Only '0' is documented; unset means auto-open. Still tri-state as a control, because 'off' must be written as 0 rather than by removing the key.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER
vectors.why: Survivor #5. 0 omits the attribution block; unset keeps it.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY
vectors.why: Survivor #6. 1 disables auto memory, 0 forces it on even when --bare or autoMemoryEnabled:false would disable it.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY
vectors.why: Survivor #7. 0 forces recaps off, 1 forces them on over the setting.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FINE_GRAINED_TOOL_STREAMING
vectors.why: Survivor #8. 0 opts out, 1 forces on when routing through a proxy.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS
vectors.why: Survivor #9. 0 reverts to TodoWrite; the version number in the prose is not a default.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT
vectors.why: Survivor #10. 1 shortens the system prompt; 0/false/no/off opts out.

vectors.name: MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING
vectors.why: Survivor #11. 0 restores the blocking connection wait. The '5-second' in the prose belongs to that wait, not to this variable, and must not be read as a default.

vectors.name: OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES
vectors.why: Survivor #12. 1 includes response text, 0 keeps it redacted, unset inherits OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS.

vectors.name: USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP
vectors.why: Survivor #13. 0 uses the system rg.

vectors.name: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H
vectors.why: Two-state toggle: only 'Set to 1' is documented, so off is unset. Also the reason the numeric-default extractor requires a connector or backticks — 'instead of the default 5 minutes' describes the prompt cache, not this variable, and used to be reported as default '5'.

vectors.name: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER
vectors.why: Two-state toggle carrying Claudepot's own disable_updates hazard while sitting in CC's pre-trust-safe allowlist — attributes are orthogonal, not tiers.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_CONNECT_IDE
vectors.why: The second toggle vocabulary. Its doc states both `false` (prevent) and `true` (force), so it is a tri-state — and it shipped as free text, a boolean rendered as an open box. The offered literals are the ones its own doc uses: writing `1` where the doc says `true` would be guessing at a value.

vectors.name: OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_VERSION
vectors.why: Two-state in the true/false vocabulary: only `true` is documented and the default is excluded, so off means removing the key rather than writing `false`.

vectors.name: OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID
vectors.why: The mirror image — only `false` is documented, default included — so off IS a value and unset is a third state.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL
vectors.why: The enum-drift case. Its own prose lists six values; ENUM_OVERRIDES carried four, so the docs never 'deferred to another page' here and the override was silently dropping max and auto. Derived from prose now, and the superset assertion fails loudly if an override ever undercuts prose again.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_DEBUG_LOG_LEVEL
vectors.why: A closed 'Values:' set the old parenthetical-only extractor missed, so it shipped as a free-text field.

vectors.name: ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER
vectors.why: Enum via the parenthetical fallback rather than a 'Values:' clause — both paths stay covered.

vectors.name: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH
vectors.why: Must NOT become an enum. Its documented values include the parametric auto:N (example auto:5); closing the set to true/auto/false would reject a legal value — the same sin as inventing numeric bounds.

vectors.name: ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS
vectors.why: Overlap case 1, and the proof that CC's SAFE_ENV_VARS cannot double as a disclosure judgement: pre-trust-safe AND able to carry 'Authorization: Bearer ...' in its documented Name: Value format.

vectors.name: ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY
vectors.why: Overlap case 2: pre-trust-safe, provider-managed, and a credential.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS
vectors.why: The regex false positive the old sensitive rule produced. It is a refresh interval, and CC lists it as pre-trust-safe — a value the pane must be able to show.

vectors.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
vectors.why: Secret plus a hazard from CC's own taxonomy (switch to attacker-controlled project).

vectors.name: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
vectors.why: CC's redirect-to-attacker-controlled-server class.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE
vectors.why: Claudepot's execute-arbitrary-code class, which CC's comment does not enumerate. Read per Bash command rather than at bootstrap, so it stays editable — unlike CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
vectors.why: Blocked. CC resolves its config directory from process.env before settings load and memoizes it, then applies settings.env over it — some paths resolve against the old directory, later ones against the new. Read-only with 'set this in your shell'.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID
vectors.why: Blocked for the other reason: host-injected per run, never user-set. Still rendered, read-only, so a hand-set key is never invisible.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS
vectors.why: An ordinary number with no zero-is-special prose — the control class must not depend on that prose existing.

vectors.name: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_DESCRIPTION
vectors.why: Why `format` is a hint and never validation: this is prose, and the MODEL-in-name rule labels it model-id. Validating against the hint would reject legitimate values.

vectors.name: CLAUDE_AFK_COUNTDOWN_MS
vectors.why: The docs' bare-backtick default form, 'Default `20000` (20 seconds)' — distinct from the parenthetical and colon forms, and the one the stricter extractor almost dropped.
